content:
[L] high | top-left window edge | "Knowledge" heading and all header text are clipped at the very left and top edges with zero inset — heading touches the window border.
[L] high | header/banner region | setup instruction text runs full-width edge-to-edge and is clipped at the left window border ("Help Center sync needs..." starts cut off).
[S] high | whole content area | every region (heading, subtitle, warning, tabs, table) is flush against the window edge with no shared margin or container padding.
[C] high | bottom ~55% of screen | vast empty black/void dead zone below the two-row table — content occupies only the top of a tall window, reading as a debug tool.
[H] high | global typography | heading, subtitle, warning, table text, and tabs all render at near-identical small size and weight; no heading scale anywhere.
[H] med | warning line under title | the setup warning (a primary action driver) is styled as plain body text with no emphasis, icon, or affordance.
[H] med | table SOURCE column | "#1" values are raw internal IDs exposed as user-facing data — debug output, not product copy.
[S] med | table row buttons | Read/Edit buttons and "More" controls sit at inconsistent offsets; "More" caret floats with unequal gap versus button pairs.
[S] med | tab bar vs table | tab underline and table left edges do not share a grid — table header inset differs from the tab text inset.
[H] med | column headers | ALL-CAPS micro-labels (TITLE, SOURCE, VISIBILITY, CHUNKS, ACTIONS) at very small size are hard to read and overuse caps.
[S] low | Sync button | top-right "Sync Help Center now" button has inconsistent margins versus the left-flush header stack.
[C] low | table | two rows in an unbounded full-width table with no container, border, or card treatment — no visual grouping of the table region.
[C] low | "Import documents" disclosure | collapsed floating disclosure triangle with no surrounding container or spacing rhythm ties it to the table below.

VERDICT: unprofessional — clipped edge-flush text, a half-black empty screen, raw "#1" debug values, and flat uniform typography fail any commercial desktop standard.

Note: the two table rows themselves are internally readable.
